data.name: Kishori
data.gender_notes: Kishori is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit words ‘Kishor’ meaning youthful and ‘I’ meaning ‘in’. Kishori represents the embodiment of youthful beauty, grace, and joy. In Hindu mythology, Kishori is an aspect of the goddess Parvati, who is worshipped for her enchanting beauty and nurturing qualities. The name Kishori carries the meaning “Goddess of beauty and grace” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kishori usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of beauty and grace and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine feminine energy, beauty, and nurturing qualities.
data.etymology: Kishori belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of beauty and grace.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kishori total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name 'Kishori' lies in its association with the divine consort of Lord Shiva, Goddess Parvati.
